summary.headline: INOX India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 26.6% YoY to INR467 crores, with record order backlog of INR2,268 crores, but Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 21.3%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR467 crores (+26.6% YoY) and EBITDA was INR100 crores (+10.8% YoY), with a 21.3% margin and PAT of INR66 crores (+7.8% YoY). H1 FY27 was a record: total income INR849 crores, EBITDA INR189 crores at 22.3% margin, and PAT INR127 crores. Management attributed the Q2 margin dip to aggressive pricing on standard tanks, freight and geopolitical costs, and said it is not structural. Order backlog hit a record INR2,268 crores at September 30, 2026, 72% from exports, with a large US space order (about INR1,100 crores) driving lumpiness.

financial_highlights.change: Management also cited INR384 crores net cash

segments.name: Industrial gas solutions
segments.commentary: Orders of about INR60 crores from domestic players for transport equipment, train tanks and large storage tanks. More than 1,500 liquid cylinders dispatched in H1 FY27 (worth over INR25 crores) versus 1,600 last year; company claims it is the only Indian player making liquid cylinders.

segments.name: LNG solutions
segments.commentary: Combined order for 40-plus LNG semi-trailers, INR14 crores order for storage tank vaporisation and unloading pump kits, an LNG fuelling station order from a city gas distributor, and 4 LNG-train orders for Indian Railways (2 dispatched).

segments.name: Cryo-Scientific and advanced engineering
segments.commentary: About INR35 crores order for LIGO-India cryogenic equipment in Maharashtra and about INR12 crores for European TCWS piping prefabrication. Initial piping order for a Dholera semiconductor fab (Tata Electronics) has begun execution; size not disclosed.

segments.name: Space and aerospace
segments.commentary: Order book includes about INR1,100 crores from space customers, mainly one US aerospace customer (16 subcoolers and 16 large tanks, over INR1,000 crores per management). Two tanks dispatched; 10-15% of the order to be executed by March 2027 and 80-90% by March 2028.

segments.name: Beverage kegs
segments.commentary: Beverage keg sales grew about 446% YoY in Q2 FY27 and order book grew about 155% YoY. Entered a 3-year global supply agreement with a leading brewer (about 4 lakh kegs required in 2027 across 22 countries, shared with multiple vendors). Approved by 4 of 5 targeted global beverage companies.

guidance_outlook: Management says the Q2 margin dip is not structural and expects margins to return within range; H1 margin of 22.3% cited as within expected range.
Management guided to a 21-24% EBITDA margin range; CEO said 'hopefully, yes' when asked if it can be achieved.

Space order margins expected to be better than standard products; freight is in customer scope (FAS or ex-works) so freight pressure is not expected on this project. CEO said margins will improve because of this order.
Business expected to grow at least 18-20% a year, with faster growth if bigger opportunities come.
Dholera semiconductor bids for ultra-high purity and bulk gas scopes; results expected in 4-6 weeks.
ISRO third launch pad tender expected in a few months; semi-cryogenic engine test facility bid awaiting outcome; ISRO project size publicly about INR3,850 crores, possibly 10-15% higher.
capex_capacity: Savli plant had about 50% space still available after expansion two years ago; Kandla (near port) land acquired, construction expected to finish around March 2027.
Funding is from internal accruals; company is debt-free with net cash of INR384 crores and says no capex constraint.
Liquid cylinder manufacturing unit revamped; production ramped up meaningfully in H1 FY27.
Data centre cooling prototype designed; conceptualisation expected to take 6-8 months.
Automation: 60-70% of welding and fabrication is automated; SemiOrbit welding centre to supply 30-40 welders a month; company training 40-50 welders and fitters.
demand_pricing: Order backlog INR2,268 crores; management says Q2 order inflow of over INR1,000 crores was bulky and lumpy and not expected to repeat at the same pace.
About 30-40% of backlog is standard equipment; the balance is custom-built, which carries better margins.
Standard tanks face global competition; management admitted offering competitive pricing to win market share this quarter, which it said is not a regular feature.
Around 50% of backlog is from 2-3 major customers; rest is back-to-back contracts with price pass-through discussions.
India semiconductor: about INR1.6 lakh crore of projects approved, around 70% of activity in Gujarat (Dholera, Sanand).
Private Indian space startups: management projects INR2,000-3,000 crores over 3-5 years; orders received from all top startups, deliveries to about 4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin decline (ex other income about 19.5%, down about 230 bps YoY) a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the dip reflects rate and strategic pricing plus geopolitical and credit issues, is not structural, and H1 margin of 22.3% is within range.

qa_highlights.question: Why aggressive pricing when the business is complex and specialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard tanks face worldwide competition, so competitive pricing is used to hold market share; non-standard custom tanks earn better margins. Management said this quarter's pricing is not expected to be a regular feature.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and value of the US space order and what follows?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is over INR1,000 crores (16 subcoolers and 16 tanks); 10-15% to finish by March 2027 and 80-90% by March 2028. Management expects 3-4 more projects from the same customer over 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the US space order margins and freight be a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: The order is FAS or ex-works, so freight sits with the customer. Management expects margins to improve from this order and sees execution risk mitigated by planning, imported forgings and trained welders.

qa_highlights.question: Are beverage keg utilisation targets of 50-60% by year-end on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track. Four of five targeted breweries have approved the product; the fifth audit is expected in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Indian LVM3 and ISRO tenders progress?
qa_highlights.answer: ISRO visited the site and assessed capability; the company believes it is technically qualified but formal declaration is pending. Management believes competitors lack cryogenic experience.

risks_watch: Q2 EBITDA margin of 21.3% (19.5% ex other income) below the 21-24% guided range; watch whether Q3 recovers.
Lumpy order book: about INR1,100 crores concentrated in one US space customer; execution of first-of-its-kind subcoolers involves imported forgings and orbital welding.
Freight and logistics cost pressure, geopolitical conflict in West Asia, and pricing pressure on standard tanks.
Skilled manpower shortage (welders, fitters) as order book grows.

Pending decisions: ISRO third launch pad and semi-cryogenic tests, Dholera semiconductor larger bids (4-6 weeks), Andaman and Nicobar LNG tender (2-3 weeks), LIGO-India site works (L&T), and fifth brewery approval.
Credit issues flagged by management as having increased in the last quarter; no details given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and balance sheet, but defensive and hedged on Q2 margins, attributing the dip to pricing, freight and geopolitics. Repeatedly gave qualitative answers ('hopefully', 'let us see') on ISRO timing, margin guidance and order sizes not disclosed.
key_quotes: The margin dip is a mix of rate and strategic pricing and is not structural.
Our order backlog crossed INR2,200 crores, making it the highest level in the company's history.
And we will be delivering those equipment by next financial year March, that is 2028 March, okay.
So we are quite straight into this, at least for this project.

adds.what: Kandla (near port) plant on newly acquired land; construction expected to finish around March 2027

growth.why: Management guides business growth of at least 18-20% a year, backed by a record INR2,268 crore order backlog (about 1,100 crore US space order, 10-15% executed by March 2027 and 80-90% by March 2028) and Kandla plant construction due around March 2027; Savli has about 50% spare space, but guidance lacks quantified capacity timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 21.3% (about 19.5% ex other income) versus H1 22.3% and a 21-24% guided range; management calls the dip not structural and says the US space order (freight in customer scope) should improve margins, but the CEO's 'hopefully' on hitting the range and 30-40% standard-product mix under competitive pricing keep it hedged.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kandla plant construction is expected to finish around March 2027 on newly acquired land, while Savli still has about 50% spare space, so new capacity is guided but timing is not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides business growth of at least 18-20% a year against a record INR2,268 crore backlog, with the US space order 10-15% executed by March 2027 and 80-90% by March 2028; keg utilisation targeted at 50-60% by year-end.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says there is no capex constraint and funds come from internal accruals with INR384 crores net cash, but no new capex plan beyond Kandla has been announced and Savli has about 50% space spare, so a fresh announcement is conditional on bids such as ISRO or Dholera winning.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Growth guidance is 18-20% minimum with faster growth if bigger opportunities come, and ISRO third launch pad (about INR3,850 crores, possibly 10-15% higher) and Dholera semiconductor bids (results in 4-6 weeks) could lift it, but neither is confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin of 21.3% sits below the 21-24% range, freight and West Asia costs persist, standard tanks face price competition, and management flagged rising credit issues without detail.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Beverage keg 3-year global supply agreement (about 4 lakh kegs needed in 2027) with 4 of 5 targeted breweries approved and the fifth audit pending; data centre cooling is only a prototype with 6-8 months of conceptualisation.

rows.label: US space order execution ramp (INR1,100 crore)
rows.why: Order over INR1,000 crore (16 subcoolers, 16 tanks) is already under execution, with two tanks dispatched and 3-4 further projects from the same customer expected over 3-5 years.

rows.label: Semiconductor and ISRO bid outcomes
rows.why: About INR1.6 lakh crore of semiconductor projects approved with 70% in Gujarat, and the ISRO third launch pad project is about INR3,850 crore, but both outcomes are pending.

rows.label: Standard tank pricing pressure
rows.why: Management admitted competitive pricing on standard tanks (30-40% of backlog) was a one-off to hold share and said it will not be a regular feature, which points to margins recovering.
